$comment: Atrium's classification of the capability surface Hermes PUBLISHES about itself (`GET /v1/capabilities`, vendored as ../0.19.0/rest-contract.json). `hermes-features-coverage.test.ts` asserts the BIJECTION with that contract, so a version declaring a new capability turns CI red until someone says what Atrium does with it. ASYMMETRY WITH OPENCLAW, stated rather than smoothed over: OpenClaw announces an EVENT catalogue at handshake and Atrium used to drop it (G-70); Hermes announces BOOLEAN capabilities and Atrium already reads them at runtime — what was missing here was never the reading, it was the classification. The tallies live in `counts` below, DERIVED and asserted by the ratchet.

chat_completions.note: Declared and unread. Nothing in the bridge builds `/v1/chat/completions`; the REST transport posts to `/api/sessions/{id}/chat/stream`, which is `session_chat_streaming`. The earlier `handled` here confused session-chat with the announced chat-completions API, so a drift or a removal of that real surface would raise nothing (review pass 5).

chat_completions_streaming.note: Same confusion as chat_completions: the streaming Atrium consumes is session-chat's, not this API's.

responses_api.note: The Responses-style surface is declared and Atrium calls none of it: the REST transport speaks chat-completions only. Not a defect today — the turn works — but it means a capability the gateway offers is invisible to the compat manifest, so nothing would notice if it became the supported path.

responses_streaming.note: Same surface as responses_api: declared, unused, unrepresented in the manifest.

run_submission.note: Atrium submits turns through session chat, never the run-submission surface. Declared and unused; a deployment that only offered runs would fail with no diagnostic naming this.

run_status.note: Declared and unread. The Hermes client builds this URL family only for `POST /v1/runs/{id}/stop`; there is no status GET anywhere in client, turn or dispatch. A lost stream is settled through `session.resume` on the WS surface instead, so the REST recovery this capability offers is unused — and the earlier `handled` claim here was simply false (review pass 4).

run_events_sse.note: The SSE event stream is declared and unused: the default transport is WS and the alternate REST path reads its own stream. This is the surface a future REST-only deployment would need, and nothing tracks it.

run_stop.by: the Stop path (`client.ts stopRun`, called from `dispatch.ts` and `turn.ts`). STATED LIMIT, and it is upstream's: run ids minted by `/api/sessions/{id}/chat/stream` are registered in neither map `/v1/runs/{id}/stop` consults, so on the REST transport the call is a STRUCTURAL 404. Lot 45 exists so Atrium reports that as `ineffective` instead of pretending the turn was stopped. Kept `handled` rather than `gap` because Atrium does call it — marking it `gap` would claim the opposite — and the incompatibility is named here rather than hidden behind the verdict (review pass 5).

tool_progress_events.by: tool phases the normalizer turns into tool.status

approval_events.by: the blocking prompts lot 33 refuses to leave unanswered

session_resources.note: Declared and unread. Agent files reach Atrium through the dashboard's /api/files* surface (lot 47), which `hermes serve` alone does not deploy — so a resource surface the API server DOES publish is going unused while the feature it would serve degrades to a named 404.

session_chat.by: the WS transport's turn dispatch — `ws-turn.ts` submits the prompt with `prompt.submit`, the default path. (The earlier anchor pointed at `session.resume` inside `harvestLostReply`, a RECOVERY path: it satisfied the rule while citing the wrong mechanism — review pass 6.)

session_fork.note: Declared and unread. Atrium's chat branching copies the transcript and starts a FRESH session (`promptWithFreshSessionHistory`); nothing posts to the gateway's fork endpoint. The application-level fork may well stay the intended behaviour, but calling it a consumption of this capability hid the endpoint from drift detection.

admin_config_rw.why: declared FALSE by this build, and Atrium never administers a gateway's config

jobs_admin.why: declared FALSE by this build; job administration is operator business outside Atrium

memory_write_api.why: declared FALSE by this build; agent memory is the agent's own, never written by Atrium

skills_api.note: Declared TRUE and read by nothing. Atrium surfaces agents, models and skills for OpenClaw; the Hermes equivalent is offered and unused, so the two providers are not at parity on a surface the UI already has.

audio_api.why: declared FALSE by this build; Atrium's voice surface is browser-side (TTS + dictation)

realtime_voice.why: declared FALSE by this build; the realtime talk mode is an OpenClaw surface today

session_continuity_header.note: Declared and unsent. Continuity is carried by session IDS in the URL and in WS RPCs; the REST headers the client builds are Authorization, Content-Type and Accept only. Calling this handled asserted a consumption that does not exist (review pass 5).

session_key_header.note: Declared and unsent, like session_continuity_header. Per-chat isolation is enforced by the session key embedded in the identifiers, never by this header.

cors.why: a browser concern; the bridge is a server-side client and never issues cross-origin requests
